record.paper_title: Euclidean random matrices: solved and open problems
record.original_question: How can one determine whether Euclidean random matrix models have a phase in which supersymmetry is spontaneously broken, and what are the physical effects of such breaking if that phase exists?

evidence.quote: • How to find out if there is a phase where supersymmetry is spontaneously broken and which are the physical effects of such a breaking.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Euclidean random matrix models defined as follows. Let $\{x_1,\dots,x_N\}$ be $N$ points drawn independently and uniformly at random from a region of $\mathbb{R}^d$ of volume $V$, with fixed density $\rho=N/V$. Given a (deterministic) pair function $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$, form the $N\times N$ Euclidean random matrix $M$ with entries
$$M_{ij}=\delta_{ij}\sum_{k\ne i}f(x_i-x_k)-(1-\delta_{ij})f(x_i-x_j),$$
or more general variants whose entries are functions of the relative positions $x_i-x_j$. Such models possess a hidden supersymmetric structure that can be exposed by representing their resolvent and spectral observables as integrals over commuting and anticommuting (Grassmann) variables, yielding a graded action invariant under a supersymmetry that rotates bosonic and fermionic replicas into each other.

Problem. Determine whether, in the thermodynamic limit $N,V\to\infty$ with $\rho$ fixed, there exists a region of parameter space (i.e., a choice of density $\rho$, dimension $d$, and pair function $f$) in which this supersymmetry is spontaneously broken, in the sense that the supersymmetric Ward identities fail and the order parameter associated with the symmetry acquires a nonzero expectation value. If such a broken-supersymmetry phase exists, identify its physical consequences for the spectral density, the localization properties of eigenvectors, and the low-frequency behavior of dynamical correlation functions of the model.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returns related work on spontaneous supersymmetry breaking in matrix models and on the supersymmetry method in random matrix theory (e.g., Kanamori–Sugino, Kuroki–Sugino, Zirnbauer), but no source was found that conclusively establishes or rules out the existence of a spontaneously broken-supersymmetry phase specifically for Euclidean random matrix ensembles defined by random points in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The question therefore appears to remain open / unresolved in the literature accessible via search.

status_evidence.title: Spontaneous supersymmetry breaking by large-N matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Concrete models where supersymmetry is preserved for any finite N but gets broken at infinite N.
status_evidence.claim: Related but distinct: SUSY breaking studied in large-N matrix models, not the Euclidean random matrix ensembles in question.

status_evidence.title: Euclidean lattice simulation for dynamical supersymmetry breaking
status_evidence.snippet: Global supersymmetry is spontaneously broken iff ground-state energy is strictly positive; observed in Euclidean lattice simulations.
status_evidence.claim: Methodological relation: criteria for spontaneous SUSY breaking in Euclidean settings, but in lattice gauge models rather than ERM.

status_evidence.title: The Supersymmetric Method in Random Matrix Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Review of supersymmetry as a tool in random matrix theory using duality between ordinary and superspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms SUSY plays a structural role in random matrix theory but does not resolve existence of a broken-SUSY phase for ERM.
